ledgerReconciliation.L-01: CONFIRMED LIVE. Re-quantified: zero-payment floor ALONE only triggers on sub-micro-dollar dust yield (see analysis in ECON-01). NOT independently profitable (gas + NFT cost >> dust). Correctly stays Low as a standalone. REFUTES the pattern-matcher's PATTERN-002 suggestion to re-weigh up — BUT note L-01 is the *mechanism* weaponized by ECON-01 when a strategy token is misconfigured.
ledgerReconciliation.L-02: CONFIRMED LIVE (phlimbo standing-allowance depletion bricks claim). Not re-raised as new; see ECON-04 note. collectReward fixed-amount pull verified in IPhlimbo.
ledgerReconciliation.L-03: CONFIRMED (NatSpec pay-then-skim vs code skims-then-pays). Economically benign (atomic; payment priced off actual skim). Not re-raised.
ledgerReconciliation.C-01: Owner config centralization (unbounded normalizedExchangeRate, 100% discount). SUPPRESSED per known issues #4/#5. NOT re-escalated. ECON-01 is a DISTINCT non-obvious footgun (silent unsafe default), not the owner-drain framing.

findings.title: Unconfigured non-18-decimal strategy token is silently treated as 18-dec 1:1, letting a claimer drain that strategy's full real yield for ~0 payment (decimal-config footgun + zero-payment floor)
findings.type: decimal-mispricing / cross-contract value-conservation break / footgun-enabled value drain
findings.severityRationale: C4 value-leak with a stated precondition (an owner config omission), so Medium rather than unconditional High. BUT the IMPACT magnitude is High (full uncompensated yield of the misconfigured strategy, repeatable) and the failure is SILENT and FAIL-OPEN (no revert), so the root-cause default deserves High-priority remediation. Per Law 3 this is an in-scope non-obvious owner FOOTGUN that unknowingly enables a Law-1 value-extraction exploit — not the suppressed 'malicious owner drains' framing (C-01).
findings.rootCause: Both _normalizeAmount (L586-609) and _denormalizeAmount (L617-640) treat an UNCONFIGURED token (decimals==0 && normalizedExchangeRate==0, the default struct state) as 18-decimal / 1:1 passthrough. Neither addYieldStrategy(strategy, token) (L227) nor setRewardToken(_rewardToken) (L360) requires or derives a token config, and there is no deployment script in the submodule that wires it (verified: no script/ dir). So a registered strategy whose <18-dec token was never passed to setTokenConfig is silently under-normalized by 10**(18-decimals). The fail-open default (return raw instead of revert-on-unconfigured) is the core defect.
findings.economicImpact: For a strategy underlying with fewer than 18 decimals (e.g. USDT/USDC = 6) left unconfigured, _normalizeAmount under-counts its delivered yield by 10**(18-dec) = 1e12x. The skim loop still delivers the FULL real underlying to the claimer (skimSurplus(token, msg.sender), L484 — delivery is independent of SYA's pricing), but totalNormalizedYield collapses to a dust value, the discount math floors actualPayment to 0 (the L-01 floor, now weaponized), and the claimer walks away with the real yield for ZERO rewardToken. The protocol/phlimbo/Limbo stakers receive nothing for yield they were owed (1-discount) of. Symmetric brick variant: an unconfigured <18-dec REWARD token (e.g. setRewardToken(USDC) without setTokenConfig(USDC,6,..)) over-charges by 1e12x so safeTransferFrom reverts and ALL claims brick (fail-safe but a full availability outage of the core function).
findings.attackScenario:
Drain variant (value loss):
1. Owner calls addYieldStrategy(usdtStrategy, USDT) but forgets setTokenConfig(USDT, 6, 1e18). USDT remains decimals==0,rate==0.
2. usdtStrategy accrues, say, 10 USDT surplus (underlyingReceived = 10e6).
3. Attacker (holding 1 claim NFT) calls claim(idx, 0, exemptStrategies=[all OTHER correctly-configured strategies]) to ISOLATE the misconfigured one (exemptStrategies, L473, lets them do exactly this).
4. skimSurplus delivers 10 USDT to attacker. _normalizeAmount(10e6, USDT) returns 10e6 (passthrough), so totalNormalizedYield = 10e6 (== 1e-11 'USD' in 18-dec terms).
5. claimerPayment = 10e6 * 9800/10000 = 9.8e6. actualPayment = _denormalizeAmount(9.8e6, USDC[6dec]) = 9.8e6 / 1e12 = 0.
6. minRewardTokenSupplied default 0 => 0 < 0 is false, passes. transferFrom pulls 0. nudge/phlimbo both 0 (skipped).
7. emit RewardsClaimed(attacker, 0, 1). Attacker received 10 USDT for FREE. Repeat every time surplus accrues (bounded only by NFT supply + gas, both << $10).
Numbers: each 18-dec micro of normalized yield below 1e12 denormalizes to 0 USDC; the whole misconfigured-strategy payment lives in that dead zone.
findings.quantification: Standalone L-01 floor (correctly-configured tokens) only zeroes payment when discounted normalized yield < 1e12 wei-18 = 1e-6 USD (one USDC unit) — i.e. dust, never profitable. The decimal footgun MOVES the entire payment of a misconfigured 6-dec strategy permanently into that dead zone (10 USDT normalizes to 1e-11 USD << 1e-6 USD), turning a dust-only rounding artifact into a 100%-of-yield drain. No per-strategy compounding (normalize-up is exact for dec<=18; the single denormalize floor is the only loss), so the issue is the SCALE mis-set, not accumulation.
affectedParties: indirectly all reward recipients downstream of phlimbo
findings.profitability: Drain variant: unconditionally profitable for the claimer (receives real ERC20 yield, pays 0). Bounded by NFT acquisition cost (EYE-burn gate) and gas — both far below the per-claim yield once any non-trivial surplus accrues. The attacker needs only to notice an unconfigured strategy token (public via tokenConfigs getter + on-chain strategy registry).
presentMitigations: correct setTokenConfig makes it exact (rate may be 0 OR 1e18 — both mean 1:1)
decimals<=18 bound when a config IS set

minRewardTokenSupplied could catch it IF a careful claimer set it from calculateClaimAmount — but the preview uses the SAME broken normalize so it would also quote ~0, giving the claimer no signal; and default 0 disables it
findings.suggestedMitigation: Make the unconfigured state FAIL-CLOSED, not fail-open: (a) revert in _normalizeAmount/_denormalizeAmount when a token is unconfigured (require an explicit 'configured' flag in TokenConfig distinct from decimals==0), OR (b) have addYieldStrategy require strategyTokens decimals already set and setRewardToken require the reward token configured, OR (c) add a protocol-side floor in claim() that reverts when actualPayment is below a configurable fraction of the snapshot estimate (also catches gross preview/actual divergence, PARK-06). Document a deploy checklist: every strategy token AND the reward token MUST be passed to setTokenConfig before claims are enabled.
findings.knownIssueCheck: NOT covered by the 'decimal normalization to 18 (documented design)' known issue — that blesses the 18-dec normalization MECHANISM, not the silent fail-open default for an UNCONFIGURED token nor the absence of config enforcement. Distinct from C-01 (this needs no malicious owner — a single forgotten setter).
findings.newOrReconciled: NEW (profile PARK-01 / pattern PARK-LEDGER-01); economically synthesizes with ledger L-01 (the floor is the drain mechanism).

findings.title: setNudgeSplit(>0) with nudge unset bricks every yielding claim (config-ordering availability footgun)
findings.severityRationale: Permissionless core function (claim) is fully bricked for all yielding claims, but it is owner-recoverable (set nudge or zero the split) and causes no value loss — funds are never at risk, the skim loop reverts atomically (no NFT consumed). C4 Low/QA availability footgun. Non-obvious ordering hazard => in scope under Law 3.
findings.codeSnippet:
setNudgeSplit L396: if (_split > 100) revert InvalidNudgeSplit(); // no nudge!=0 check
claim L506:        if (nudgeSplit > 0 && nudge == address(0)) revert NudgeNotConfigured();
findings.rootCause: setNudgeSplit (L396-402) does not require nudge != address(0). The consistency check is deferred to claim() (L506), AFTER the skim loop, so a benign owner who raises the split before wiring the nudge address silently arms a revert on every yielding claim.
findings.economicImpact: Yield consolidation halts entirely: no strategy surplus can be skimmed/converted, no rewards reach phlimbo, until the owner sets nudge or resets nudgeSplit to 0. Surplus continues to accrue (and the discount/MEV race resets) but is inaccessible. Pure liveness, no theft.
findings.attackScenario: 1. Owner calls setNudgeSplit(20) intending to later set the nudge recipient. 2. Every claim(...) with yield now runs the full skim loop, computes payment, then reverts NudgeNotConfigured at L506. 3. Claimers waste gas (NFT preserved by atomic rollback) and stop trying. 4. Consolidation is dead until owner remediates.
affectedParties: phlimbo / stakers (no rewards during the window)
findings.suggestedMitigation: In setNudgeSplit, require nudge != address(0) when _split > 0 (and/or in setNudgeAddress(address(0)) require nudgeSplit == 0). Fail at configuration time, not deep in the claim path.

findings.title: Preview (snapshot estimate) diverges from charged amount (actual skim) and there is no payment ceiling, so a claimer's quote-derived minRewardTokenSupplied can mislead; getTotalYield ignores per-token pause
findings.type: preview-vs-actual divergence / one-directional slippage guard / view inconsistency
findings.severityRationale: No protocol value loss and no third-party griefing (a claimer's payment always tracks the yield they actually receive, so they cannot be made to overpay relative to value received without also receiving that value). Impact is claimer-side UX/self-DoS and unreliable bot quoting. C4 Low/QA.
findings.codeSnippet: claim L501: if (actualPayment < minRewardTokenSupplied) revert InsufficientYield(); // FLOOR only, no ceiling
findings.rootCause: Previews (calculateClaimAmount L651, getYield, getTotalYield) price off the snapshot estimate _getYieldForStrategy = sum(totalBalanceOf - principalOf) over getAuthorizedClients(), while claim() prices off skimSurplus's post-redeem/post-swap underlyingReceived (L484). Per the vault CLAUDE.md these diverge — 'large in either direction' for ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy (AMM-routed). minRewardTokenSupplied (L501) is a FLOOR (min-yield proxy), so it protects against under-delivery but there is no MAX-payment ceiling; additionally getTotalYield (L738) does NOT skip tokenConfigs[token].paused whereas claim/calculateClaimAmount do, so the global view over-reports vs the claimable set.
findings.economicImpact: A claimer who pre-approves exactly the calculateClaimAmount quote can have claim() revert on safeTransferFrom when actual > preview (self-DoS, wasted gas; NFT preserved). Bots relying on getTotalYield can mis-size approvals/min because it counts paused tokens. No value leaves the protocol incorrectly — payment is always (1-discount)*value-of-delivered-yield under correct config.
findings.attackScenario: Not an attacker-driven exploit: an attacker cannot inflate the victim's actualPayment without also gifting the victim the corresponding yield (e.g. donating surplus to a strategy makes the victim PROFIT by discount*donation), so there is no profitable sandwich. The realistic failure is benign divergence: AMM strategy returns more underlying than the snapshot, claimer pays more than quoted, tx reverts if approval was tight.
affectedParties: claimers / claim bots (quote reliability, approval sizing)
findings.suggestedMitigation: Add an optional maxRewardTokenSupplied ceiling to claim() (symmetric to the floor) so claimers can bound overpay; make getTotalYield skip paused tokens for consistency with claim()/calculateClaimAmount; document that calculateClaimAmount is an estimate and to add a buffer to approvals.
findings.newOrReconciled: NEW framing (profile PARK-06 / patterns PATTERN-001, PATTERN-006); concludes no MEV/sandwich exploit — explicitly down-weighted from pattern's potential-high/medium.

findings.title: Claim and preview gas scales with (strategies x authorized-clients); if it exceeds the discount incentive, the permissionless consolidation stalls (owner/OOS-bounded DoS)
findings.severityRationale: The growable dimensions are owner-bounded (addYieldStrategy is onlyOwner) and strategy-owner-bounded (IYieldStrategy.setClient is owner-gated, so the clients[] set is NOT permissionlessly attacker-growable — correcting the static/pattern premise). No external party can force the DoS, so it is an operational footgun, not a permissionless griefing vector. C4 Low.
findings.codeSnippet: _getYieldForStrategy L556: for (i in clients = strategy.getAuthorizedClients()) { totalBalanceOf; principalOf; } // nested in preview loops
findings.rootCause: claim() loops all registered strategies (L464) calling skimSurplus once each (the per-client work is inside the OOS strategy, paid by the claimer). Previews additionally nest _getYieldForStrategy's clients[] loop (L556) inside the strategy loop (calculateClaimAmount L659, getTotalYield L740). As strategy count and per-strategy authorized-client count grow, the gas to claim — and to fetch the quote that sets minRewardTokenSupplied — rises. If total gas cost exceeds discount*pending-yield, no rational claimer claims.
findings.economicImpact: Above a gas-vs-incentive threshold the permissionless conversion simply stops being profitable, so surplus accrues unconsolidated and phlimbo stops receiving rewards. Self-correcting if the owner raises discount or prunes strategies, but until then the core mechanism is economically dead. calculateClaimAmount can also revert on gas (over-large client set) denying claimers the quote.
findings.attackScenario: No permissionless trigger (client/strategy sets are owner-authorized). Owner footgun: registering many strategies and/or strategy owners authorizing many clients silently pushes claim gas above the discount, killing the incentive. A claimer can route around ONE pathological strategy via exemptStrategies (M-04 mitigation) but cannot fix aggregate cardinality.
findings.suggestedMitigation: Document a safe-config bound on (strategy count x typical client count) vs the chosen discount; consider pagination/batched claim over a strategy subrange; keep discount tunable to track gas. exemptStrategies already mitigates single-strategy pathologies.
findings.newOrReconciled: NEW framing (profile noUnboundedLoops note; patterns PATTERN-003, SLITHER-002) — corrected to owner/OOS-bounded (not permissionless) and tied to the discount-vs-gas economic threshold.

findings.title: Permissionless first-claimer captures the entire accumulated discount in one shot, and minRewardTokenSupplied defaults to 0 (designed incentive + residual MEV note)
findings.type: MEV / first-claimer capture / default-disabled slippage guard
findings.severityRationale: This is the INTENDED incentive mechanism: the discount exists precisely to pay whoever performs the decentralized conversion, and the protocol pays exactly discount*yield regardless of WHO claims, so there is no protocol value leak beyond the by-design incentive. The residual is ordinary MEV competition (gas auction among claimers) and a foot-note that min=0 disables the per-claim floor. Informational/QA.
findings.codeSnippet: claimerPayment = totalNormalizedYield * (10000 - discountRate) / 10000; // whole accumulated pot, first-claimer-takes-all discount
findings.rootCause: claim() skims ALL non-exempt strategies' surplus and applies the discount to the whole sum in a single permissionless call (L497). Accumulated yield is a growing pot; the first valid-NFT caller captures the full discount on it. minRewardTokenSupplied defaults to caller-chosen with 0 disabling the only floor.
findings.economicImpact: No incremental protocol loss (discount is the budgeted incentive). Losers of the claim race revert with ZeroAmount (NFT preserved, gas wasted) — standard MEV race friction. A careless/bot claimer passing min=0 accepts any yield amount, including the dust/zero-payment edge (L-01) — but that harms only the claimer's own economics, not the protocol.
findings.attackScenario: Searcher backruns large surplus accrual / a paused-token unpause and wins the claim with a higher gas bid, taking the discount. This is the system working as designed (decentralized conversion incentive), not an exploit. No sandwich of a victim exists (first claim empties the pot; there is no shared post-loop balance to skim).
findings.profitability: Claiming is profitable by ~discount*yield minus gas for whoever wins — exactly the intended incentive.
findings.suggestedMitigation: None required for security. Optionally document the MEV/race expectation for integrators and recommend claim bots always pass a non-zero minRewardTokenSupplied derived from calculateClaimAmount (with a buffer) to avoid the dust/zero-payment edge.
findings.newOrReconciled: NEW framing (patterns PATTERN-007); concludes no exploit (down-weighted from potential-medium) — the discount capture is the design, and ties min=0 exposure to ledger L-01.

summary.headline: One Medium economic footgun (ECON-01) is the material finding: the fail-open 'unconfigured token => 18-dec 1:1 passthrough' default turns an owner's forgotten setTokenConfig into a silent, repeatable, full-value drain of a <18-decimal strategy's yield (claimer receives real tokens, pays 0 via the L-01 floor) — or, symmetrically, bricks all claims if the reward token is the unconfigured one. The remaining findings are Low/QA liveness footguns (ECON-02 nudge-split brick, ECON-04 gas-vs-discount stall) and benign/by-design observations (ECON-03 preview divergence with no exploitable sandwich, ECON-05 first-claimer MEV is the intended incentive).
severityRanked: Medium  ECON-01  decimal-config fail-open => free strategy-yield drain / claim brick (NEW; weaponizes L-01)
Low     ECON-02  nudgeSplit>0 + unset nudge bricks claims (NEW footgun)
Low     ECON-03  preview-vs-actual divergence + no payment ceiling + getTotalYield pause inconsistency (NEW; no sandwich)
Low     ECON-04  claim/preview gas scales with strategies x clients vs discount => consolidation stall (NEW; owner/OOS-bounded, not permissionless)
QA      ECON-05  first-claimer discount-capture MEV is by-design; min=0 default ties to L-01 (informational)
explicitlyNotEscalated: Owner-drain via 100% discount / unbounded exchange rate => C-01 (suppressed, known issues #4/#5). NOT re-raised.
L-01 standalone zero-payment => stays Low (re-quantified: dust-only, not profitable alone). NOT re-escalated; only ECON-01 weaponizes it.
L-02 phlimbo allowance brick / L-03 doc-impl mismatch => confirmed live, reconcile to ledger, not re-raised as new.
PATTERN-001 principal-skew / PATTERN-006 missing-slippage => no protocol-side value leak in-scope (payment tracks actual delivery); folded into ECON-03 at Low.
summary.valueConservationVerdict: Under CORRECT config, value is conserved: nudgeAmount + phlimboAmount == actualPayment exactly (subtraction-derived, no dust), and actualPayment == (1-discount)*normalized(actual delivered yield). The ONLY conservation break is ECON-01 (misconfig) which lets delivered yield exceed charged payment by up to 100%.
